2026-08-13 stage-3 decision plane + flush BUILT (1f65bc1..ed04b08 = 24 commits, plus the record commits, subagent-driven, per-task reviews + fix rounds on tasks 9/10/12/13/14/15): decided set is an open-addressed slot table over an insertion-ordered ring, not a map - each id+deadline is stored once and the ring's head order IS deadline order per shard, making expiry exact-W and O(1) amortized; 41.9 B/entry at the gated 1M population against the map-keyed sketch's 65.4, but the HONEST envelope is 40-64 B/entry across the power-of-two sawtooth (the ring holds up to ~2x live just above a growth boundary) and capacity sizing uses ~64, per ADR-009 r8; keep events ride the shard work queue so a verdict stays single-writer and the set answers duplicates - decisions are exactly-once (no duplicate flush or publish), spans are at-least-once by contract (ADR-009 r5, backend dedup is the backstop); worker-collects/flusher-exports split: workers hand FlushJobs down a channel and park un-done need-bits in a per-shard pending map when it is full, retrying them on the 1s tick - and that map is DECIDED to need no hard bound TODAY: it is unbounded by structure and deduped by trace id, and what actually bounds it is that Loopback.Publish cannot fail - NeedFlush intents drain against decided entries that W-evict, but NeedPublish intents SURVIVE that eviction and would retry forever through a publish outage longer than W, unreachable until the stage-6 real bus lands; the pending.flushes gauge is the alarm rather than a refusal path; while the flusher is the processor's SINGLE emission point holding every unbounded-latency step (Publish, fragmenter.Decode, ConsumeTraces) off the ingest path;
